income_kind: per-day array of number or null
words: Series contract 0.3.0 (DB-b-278, with Amendment 1 of the same order) adds two optional series fields, unreported_trading_days (the ISO dates of the window's trading days the source did not report, [] when none) and unreported_trading_days_basis (the fixed text 'trading calendar minus present partitions'), both carried from the report-build handler's unreported_days statement, and a top-level unreported_days_rule of five sentences. Amendment 1 changes only series.fields.income: its kind becomes per-day array of number or null, null exactly where the source's income_received is null, and a null is never read as zero. Every earlier series still validates: a series with neither new field, and a series whose income array holds numbers, both pass the reference validator. On a series from a source that carries the statement the two fields are a pair and are always present, the list being [] when there are none. Not proven: that any publisher writes these fields (the Cottonwood publish cell's), that the page reads them or mirrors the contract (the page's cell, whose parity test is not graded here), and that the income null rule holds on any live series.
